opening_message:
Ticket 1: Donna Ball (employee ID E024) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E024.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Donna Ball (E024) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write access (admin requires owning role; Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code), so write is within policy.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Donna Ball (E024) is a contractor with basic security training (noting a conflict with the earlier note listing full_time). Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training (never admin). Basic training means write is above the maximum, so recommend read for Source Code.
reason: There is conflicting employee data for Donna Ball (E024). Note 1 (HR) lists her as full_time, which would allow write for Source Code. Note 2 (Security DB) lists her as a contractor with basic security training and explicitly flags the conflict with the earlier note. Under the contractor classification, write requires advanced security training; with basic training the maximum allowed access is read, and contractors can never have admin. Because the Security DB note provides the more specific, explicitly-corrected current record and granting write would violate policy if the contractor status is correct, I grant the maximum allowed under that classification: read.

- contractor: read, or write if advanced training. Never admin. Basic training → write not allowed → max read.
